body: @Antonialock Did you have a chance to look at that ?

author: Antonialock
body:
Sorry!

I see that this annotation is added to proteins belonging to these [funfam families](https://www.uniprot.org/arba/ARBA00087037)
which hits these [laminins](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb?query=%28xref%3A%22funfam-2.10.25.10%3AFF%3A000011%22%29+AND+%28xref%3A%22funfam-2.10.25.10%3AFF%3A000065%22%29+AND+%28xref%3A%22funfam-2.10.25.10%3AFF%3A000333%22%29)

I think this lamini trimer might be ok for LAMB4? Unfortunately it's just from a preprint but it says:
Finally, we found that LAMB4/laminin β4 is necessary for actin filament accumulation and it interacts with laminin α4 and laminin γ3, forming the laminin-443, a previously unreported laminin trimer

what do you think?
(I'm guessing the annotation will disappear anyway once we take IBA into account...)

author: pgaudet
body: Interesting !! @DaiqingChen Did you see that paper ?

author: Antonialock
body:
in any case, I think this condition set (the combination of funfams, that get annotated to the GO term) will disappear once when we take IBA into account since LAMB4 [B7ZMJ6] has IBA cellular component annotations to basement membrane and extracellular space, but not laminin-121 trimer (the entry is in swiss-prot, so ARBA should see it and learn from it). 

I will put this issue on my list of rules to check back on, once we have done a release, to see that this is what happened (to my understanding this is what should happen, but we haven't done a release yet since I started doing fixes for ARBA, so I'm not 100% confident..).
